previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to a high amikacin trough level of 9.0 and inability to manage his complex IV antibiotic regimen at home. He has a history of liver transplant and recent pseudomonas bacteremia and urinary tract infection requiring prolonged antibiotic therapy. During the 3-day stay, amikacin was held initially, then restarted after a safe trough level was confirmed. Meropenem was continued with extended infusions. The patient's kidney function remained stable despite baseline acute kidney issues, and hyperkalemia was monitored without intervention. Diarrhea was evaluated and found not to be due to C. diff. Malnutrition was noted with low albumin, and nutritional support was recommended. Given his self-care limitations, discharge was arranged to an extended care facility to complete antibiotic treatment. Follow-up includes post-treatment blood and urine cultures and ongoing monitoring through the transplant clinic.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site

Brief Hospital Course:

physical therapy and refusal to take medications.  During his 
hospital stay, the patient's predominant issue remained social.

transplant medicine/surgery were involved in helping him 
understand the need for his cooperation.  Improvements were made

physical therapy.  Psychiatry visited with him on multiple 
occasions at the request of the transplant team as our concern 
was that he might be depressed.  Psychiatry did not feel that he 
was having a major depressive episode but did recommend low dose 
citalopram to help him with his irritability. The patient agreed 
to take this therefore, 10mg qd was started on ___.

Calorie counts were performed which showed waxing and waning. .

carnation instant breakfasts.

worsening of renal function which improved with hydration.  
Concomitantly, the patient required treatment for hyperkalemia 
with an increased florinef.  Nutrition reiterated the importance 
of a low potassium diet.
